source.title: How to Initialize your Network? Robust Initialization for WeightNorm & ResNets
source.authors: Devansh Arpit; Víctor Campos; Yoshua Bengio

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including supplementary material; no apparent truncation affecting the reported findings.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own CIFAR-10 training-accuracy results across initialization methods and network depths, directly bearing on initialization and depth claims, though its main measure is accuracy rather than training classification error rates stated as such.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s CIFAR-10 depth and initialization comparisons and its reported training accuracy on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100. MNIST depth results are outside the benchmark settings named by the versions. Synthetic initialization-only signal-flow measurements are not training outcomes; test-error and Hessian-curvature comparisons do not measure training error. Figure values not stated numerically in text remain figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares initialization methods and trainability across depths in plain weight-normalized ReLU networks, testing V4 in a different normalization setting. Its residual-network experiments do not establish V4's claims about plain networks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their initialization improves depth, hyperparameter, and seed robustness in weight-normalized networks, places initialization in lower-curvature regions, and, with learning-rate warmup, reduces the final-performance gap with batch normalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests initialization choices in weight-normalized networks and reports CIFAR-10 train accuracy across depths. Its intervention concerns initialization and depth, but it does not directly report the zero or near-zero training classification error claim as an error rate.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with initialization method, network depth, learning rate, and learning-rate warmup; the proposed method is reported as more robust across tested configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: In weight-normalized WRNs, proposed initialization maintains similar one-epoch accuracy across tested depths through 10,000 layers; default initialization diverges for most depths, while stage-wise Hanin needs smaller learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization and residual-branch scaling affect trainability and learning-rate tolerance in very deep weight-normalized residual networks.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 depth results are plotted rather than numerically tabulated in the supplied text. WRNs are trained for only a single epoch in the depth sweep; the full training-error values cannot be recovered from the figure text. CIFAR-100 results report test error, not training error.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 MNIST depth and hyperparameter results are outside the CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 benchmark conditions in V1 and do not directly test a listed version. Figure 3 CIFAR-10 CNN and WRN plotted accuracy results are retained only where initialization is relevant to V4; corresponding validation-accuracy curves are omitted because they duplicate the measure without a disagreement stated in text. Table 1 reports test error rather than training error. Figure 1 synthetic measurements concern signal norms at initialization rather than training outcomes. Table 2 measures Hessian spectral norm at initialization rather than training error.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error, substantial residual training error, and random or corrupted labels are not established by readable numerical results. The statement that WRN-40-10 does not completely fit its training set does not quantify its distance from near-zero error.
Teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized CNNs versus matched identity-shortcut networks; very deep plain tanh networks; and normalization-free Fixup training.
The orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparison in very deep tanh networks and training plain convolutional networks at 10,000 layers. The reported 10,000-layer experiment uses residual connections.
Training above a measured initial stability threshold, recovery with decreasing curvature, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Controlled effects of adding batch normalization on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup alternative. Final test-error comparisons do not establish these effects.

missing.what: The proposed-initialization counterparts to R1, including He and orthogonal weights, are missing. Extract their training-accuracy/depth comparisons without inventing numerical values from the text.
missing.locator: Section 5.1, convolutional networks paragraph; Figure 3 left; Appendix Table 4

record.verdict_notes: MNIST is not outside V4's scope. The explicitly declared Figure 2 omission removes relevant evidence: data-dependent initialization trains through depth 20 but diverges at greater depths, whereas the proposed initialization trains through 200 layers and permits larger learning rates. No additional missing entry is added for this already-declared omission. Failures of baseline initializations do not challenge a claim that appropriately matched initialization improves trainability. Exact training accuracies cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100 training error, or whether sufficiently large networks reach zero or near-zero training classification error.
Two-layer teacher-student ReLU networks and student width relative to teacher width are not studied.

The study compares depth effects in CIFAR-10 convolutional and residual networks, but does not compare plain batch-normalized networks against otherwise identical residual networks or test whether shortcuts prevent training-error degradation. Its CIFAR-10 accuracy plots do not provide textual training-error results suitable for extraction as rows.

The paper tests initialization effects on CIFAR-10 convolutional and residual networks; it does not test the cited orthogonal Gaussian tanh initialization comparison or train plain CNNs at 10,000 layers.
Learning rates above a stability limit, loss-curvature dynamics during training, and full-batch sharpness behavior are not tested.

The paper compares weight normalization with batch normalization, but does not test whether adding batch normalization speeds training or increases learning-rate tolerance. Fixup is only cited as prior work.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 CNN+WN, data-dependent (He)
rows.operation_detail: Depth sweep comparing initialization methods; train and validation accuracy reported in Figure 3.
rows.note: The text says the data-dependent initialization fails at optimizing very deep networks; exact plotted train-accuracy values are not stated. State reflects the stated failure at greater depth, not a numerical error-rate estimate.
rows.check: Failure of an unsuitable initialization at greater depth is evidence for initialization-dependent trainability, not itself a limitation of V4. The explicit depth-20 cutoff and divergence at learning rate 10^-5 concern MNIST MLPs, not this CIFAR-10 CNN row. For CNNs, the text states only that data-dependent initialization fails on very deep networks; exact accuracies are unavailable.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, convolutional-networks paragraph; Figure 3 left and caption; supplementary Table 4.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 WRN+WN, proposed (orthogonal)
rows.size_stated: k = 1; number of layers swept from 10 to 10,000
rows.operation_detail: Depth sweep comparing initialization methods; train and validation accuracy reported after one epoch.
rows.uncertainty: results over 5 random seeds for each configuration
rows.note: Authors state the proposed initialization achieves similar accuracy across evaluated depths. Training was deliberately limited to one epoch; exact plotted train-accuracy values are not stated.
rows.check: These are residual networks, whereas V4 names plain networks. Similar accuracy after one epoch through 10,000 residual layers does not establish training of 10,000-layer plain CNNs. The one-epoch condition also does not establish convergence.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 WRN+WN, PyTorch default (orthogonal)
rows.size_stated: k = 1; number of layers swept from 10 to 10,000
rows.operation_detail: Depth sweep comparing initialization methods; train and validation accuracy reported after one epoch.
rows.uncertainty: results over 5 random seeds for each configuration
rows.note: Authors state PyTorch default initialization diverges for most depths. The plotted exact values are not stated.
rows.check: The reported divergence is a valid residual-network result, but does not measure any listed version's specified comparison. It should not be labeled absent for V4.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 WRN+WN, stage-wise Hanin (orthogonal)
rows.size_stated: k = 1; number of layers swept from 10 to 10,000
rows.operation_detail: Depth sweep comparing initialization methods; train and validation accuracy reported after one epoch.
rows.uncertainty: results over 5 random seeds for each configuration
rows.note: Authors state this initialization and the proposed one achieve similar accuracy, but it requires learning rates an order of magnitude smaller. Exact plotted train-accuracy values are not stated.
rows.check: This residual-network initialization comparison does not test V4's plain-network claim. Needing a smaller learning rate is not independently evidence of slower learning or a limitation of V4.

relationships.condition: Plain weight-normalized ReLU CNNs on CIFAR-10 with initialization varied across depths
relationships.reason: R1 and the Section 5.1 comparison report failure of data-dependent initialization at large depth and better depth robustness with the proposed initialization; the proposed-method counterpart needs extraction. This supports initialization-dependent trainability in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: The proposed initialization maintained better trainability at large depths, where data-dependent initialization failed.
